first.rationale:
The two acute, measurable declines are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and onboarding friction plausibly drives both, so simplify_onboarding attacks the shared upstream cause rather than a symptom. I deliberately reject promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that it lifts acquisition and revenue but materially harms 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strongest runner-up but only addresses one of the two declines; referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist target segments that are not where the erosion is showing.

I spend the verification budget on the two memories that actually carry the decision. memory_86 is the primary load-bearing claim (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and is 24 days old with no indication of how durable or how large the effect was. memory_31 is the mechanism-level claim (cutting required signup fields) and matters because its recorded outcome is first-week activation, not retained or qualified revenue; if the original record shows the lift was measured only at week one, the memory does not license a long-horizon bet. I am not verifying memory_73 because it is being used only to rule an option out, and a weaker-than-recorded retention harm would not make promotional pricing attractive under this objective.

Downstream value risk is real and flagged: removing required signup fields can degrade lead qualification data, shift mix toward lower-intent accounts, and inflate activation metrics while lowering qualified-revenue quality — the same metric-vs-value gap that made promotional pricing look good on acquisition. It could also undercut the sales-assisted enterprise path in memory_44 if qualifying fields are what route demo requests. So I run this as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout: hold enterprise/demo-request routing out of the treatment, keep at least the fields that drive qualification, and instrument 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline quality as guardrails alongside completion and activation. All inherited findings are from prior conditions and predate the competitor's entry pricing; the current environment may have shifted the mix, so these are priors to be re-tested, not settled facts.
